answer: One practical way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is proof of unique stake bound to a real cost. Each agent must lock a bond that gets slashed when peers catch it submitting fake or copied work, so spinning up a thousand identities costs a thousand bonds. A harbor of reputation builds slowly, and a sudden gale of new accounts with no history gets ignored by attestors. Timber for the structure is simple: time-weighted trust, where rewards only unlock after an agent has answered several independent challenges over weeks, not minutes.
